text: BINT code rows (30 per new unit, unhooked, vLLM) were drawn with the committed base intents BEFORE the unit commits; BINT is content_free = false and enters only the K prices and descriptive tables, never a forecast or an L/M test.

II3: the HF-vs-vLLM twin engine check failed (JS above the template-resampling null q95); its twin baseline for the escape gate uses the 50 HF CRN slots only, and q_tail committed from all 300 twin samples is reported beside an HF-only sensitivity; II3 is not tail-empty, so L1a is unaffected (plan F4).

After the II1-II6 commits the tracer gained counters for heapq.merge / nsmallest / nlargest (pure-Python helpers that emit no c_call event) so that the II7/II8 labellers can see them; no committed II1-II6 or B-unit rule reads these counters, so their labels are unchanged.

The pod has an NVIDIA L4 (23 GB, cc 8.9) instead of the planned RTX A4500; the frozen precision rule selects W16A16 bf16 (VRAM >= 19.5 GiB). HF hooked arms ran in batches of B = 20 rows (exp26 convention), at about 7-14 s per batch.

Specs ask for 'def solve(...)' instead of LeetCode's 'class Solution' entry point, so the iteration-5 sandbox, tracer, plain-completion template and labeller backbone apply unchanged (the FORMAT_LINE of every iteration-5 unit names solve).

Commit #0 (protocol, every rule in prose) preceded the first sample; the analysis code (analysis/pool_l1.py, l2l3.py, m_k.py), the M signs, the frozen operational choices, the schema and the test log were hash-committed at 22:11:51Z, after the predictor-side samples but before the first nudge sample (22:18:33Z) -- outcomes are the nudge arms only (exp26 convention).
Model weights were read from the run's shared HF cache (HF_HUB_CACHE), not WS/hf_cache; nothing to delete in the workspace.

The mini end-to-end dry run on DRYRUN_T03 was not run; the pipeline was exercised on the committed units' own data, and the placebos of audit/rederive.py (random r_u, twin-as-nudge, base/lik swap) were run on the real events instead.

SCREEN units A1-A5, A7-A9 (exp25 newbench framework) were NOT topped up (no fresh twin of 300, q_lik or base top-up) for lack of time: integrating the second labeller framework did not fit the 6-hour budget. Their iteration-5 confirmed landing counts are reported descriptively in results/screen.json with the iteration-5 forecasts only. This misses a never-drop item of the plan; the B units (exp26 framework) were fully topped up.
BINT on the iteration-5 units was dropped (drop order item 1); GTN alpha 2, PN alpha 4 and ESC alpha 4 ran on all seven B units.

II9 (longest palindrome) and II10 (palindrome integer) were not built (time); reserves II11/II12 were not needed (five units had passed both gates by T+2:00). Eight list-II units were built; seven have a default and were enrolled.

II2 (task scheduler): the instruct twin writes the frame formula without the count of maximum-frequency letters in 249/250 programs (twin pass 0/150 at T 1.0), so the unit has NO_DEFAULT and enters no L or M test; its base and BINT samples are reported only.

Forced 'Implement X' prompts often return the default algorithm (e.g. II4 index_of_max 0 verified of 40 attempts, II6 replace_pairs and recursive_descent 0 of 40, II5 insertion_build 0 of 40); q_lik is undefined for such algorithms and they receive the frozen floor of the add-one smoothed softmax (predictions/analysis_choices.json). II6 has no scored algorithm in S, so qlik_top1 is None and II6 cannot be discordant. results/... forced_compliance per unit is in units.json.

One revision round each, before the unit commits: II6 runtime rule (the tracer's patched deque reports '_patch.<locals>.deque.append', so pushes/pops are matched by method name) and II7 (heap insertion and insert-at-front shifting are 'other'; asserts are ignored by the AST rule; backward fill needs a hot index-decrement line). Both re-gated: kappa 1.0, holdout 6/6; every row of the unit was relabelled with the revised rules before its commit.
Gate (ii) instruct gold programs are the first 10 valid twin programs (vLLM slots k >= 10) rather than separate gate draws; base gold programs are the first 10 valid base-pilot programs (chat k 0-5).

15-program base audits: labeller vs two-family adjudication below 0.85 on all valid programs for II1 (0.40), II4 (0.73), II5 (0.80) and II7 (0.73), mostly on failing base programs; on correct base programs agreement is 1.0 except II1 (4/7). These units are flagged AUDIT_WEAK and a post-hoc sensitivity drops them.

A readiness bug briefly scheduled ESC confirmation tasks before any ESC stage-1 sample existed; they found no stage-1 passers and wrote nothing. The daemon was fixed (confirmation waits for the complete stage-1 population) and restarted before the first ESC sample.
HF twin batches (k 0-9 per template) are padded to B = 20 with TWIN_EXTRA slots k 10-19; these rows are engine-check material only and never enter a decisive cell or the twin of 300.

vLLM rows use per-request seeds (sha256-derived) and are not CRN-paired with HF rows; the HF-vs-vLLM twin engine check (JS vs template-resampling null) passed for every unit except II3 (ENGINE_SPLIT).

SCREEN B units' twin of 300 = the iteration-5 HF CRN slots k 0-9 (RTX 4090, vendored labels) + 150 new vLLM T 1.0 slots + 100 vLLM T 1.3 slots; their alpha-4 escape gate uses the same T 1.0 twin. The HF re-draw of the iteration-5 slots on this GPU is the engine check (per-slot agreement in results/engine_checks.json).

II1 keeps the single-query signature solve(s, t); the plan's batch of 200 s-queries in the stress cases (to favour the position-list method) was not added. Every reference passes at <= 0.25 x the 1 s limit and the LCS table exceeds it.

Arms were not run in 10 -> 100 -> full stages: vLLM measured 7-34k programs/h and HF 7-14 s per 20-row batch in the first jobs (logs/vllm_*.log, results/timing.jsonl), and every planned arm then fit without drops except those listed here.
